N-body/dynamical-model mass, not directly used by the light-emissivity profile in this recipe; recorded for completeness and for the mass-segregation limitation below.

This is a 3D mass radius from a dynamical model, not a directly observed projected quantity. Used here (via an approximate projected/3D scaling, see projected-half-light-approx) to fix the King concentration of a separately assumed *light* profile; mass and light radii can differ under mass segregation.
Used as an approximation for the projected King core radius (approximation A in king-abel-profile.json); no independent photometric King fit for this specific radius was located in this session.

evidence.scope: Whole cluster; varies with radius across the literature (roughly 0.08 core to ~0.19 outskirts)
evidence.limitations: This is the primary evidence AGAINST the sphericity assumption used everywhere else in this ledger. Omega Centauri is a measurably flattened, rotating cluster; every quantity below that assumes spherical symmetry is only a first-order approximation to its real triaxial/oblate shape.

evidence.quantity: publisher pointing center vs. independent catalogue position
evidence.limitations: This confirms the publisher WCS center matches the independently catalogued cluster center to sub-pixel accuracy (0.24 arcsec vs. 0.21 arcsec/px). It is a whole-field sanity check, not a star-by-star astrometric fit against an external catalogue (e.g. Gaia); no such per-star fit was performed in this session.

value.formula: Sigma(R) proportional to [ (1+(R/rc)^2)^-1/2 - (1+(rt/rc)^2)^-1/2 ]^2 for R <= rt

evidence.scope: Adopted profile family for the projected light distribution
evidence.limitations: Standard single-mass isotropic empirical law; Omega Centauri has multiple stellar populations and measurable rotation/flattening that a single-mass spherical King law does not capture.

evidence.quantity: projected half-light radius as a fraction of the 3D half-mass radius
evidence.scope: Used once, to convert the measured 3D half-mass radius into a target projected half-light radius for solving the King concentration
evidence.limitations: This factor is an approximate, broadly-applicable result for centrally concentrated dispersion-supported systems, not a value measured for Omega Centauri specifically.

evidence.quantity: spherically symmetric 3D relative emissivity vs. radius, derived by Abel-inverting the fitted King projected profile
evidence.scope: 0 to the solved tidal radius (46.4 pc)
evidence.limitations: Deterministic consequence of assumed spherical symmetry plus the King profile family and its two fixed shape parameters (approximations A and B recorded in king-abel-profile.json). It is not a released, independently measured 3D point table; it is our own Abel-inversion computation from measured/published-model inputs. The single strongest physical limitation is sphericity itself: Omega Centauri's true ellipticity (~0.08-0.19, entry 'ellipticity') means the real 3D structure is oblate/triaxial, not spherical, and this profile cannot represent that flattening.

evidence.quantity: status note, not a physical quantity
evidence.limitations: The lab's only currently implemented method that treats an external prior as 'broad shape from the prior, detail fitted from the image' (simulation-guided-finite-emission@1 / two-scale) requires a pre-existing fixed-density Alignment reconstruction (a 'baselineId') built from an N-body particle simulation via prepare-full-density. No such simulation or baseline exists for a globular cluster, and building one would mean writing new object-preparation tooling, which this task explicitly excludes. See README.md.
